chunks: I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! What are you (plural)?' He said: 'We are the treasurers of Allah's knowledge, and we are the translators of Allah's revelation, and we are the conclusive proof upon those beneath the sky and above the earth.'

key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ الْبَالِغَةُ: The conclusive/complete proof — a Quranic concept (6:149) meaning irrefutable authority; the Imams are God's definitive argument over all creation
key_terms.تَرَاجِمَةُ وَحْيِ اللَّهِ: Translators/interpreters of Allah's revelation — the Imams explain and convey the meaning of divine revelation to humanity
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be sacrificed for you — a conventional expression of deep reverence and devotion used by companions when addressing the Imams
key_terms.خُزَّانُ عِلْمِ اللَّهِ: Treasurers/custodians of Allah's knowledge — the Imams are described as the repositories of the full divine knowledge transmitted by the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say when asked 'What are you?' regarding the Imams' role?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Sadyr al-Sayrafi asks Imam al-Baqir (AS) the profound question: 'What are you?' The Imam responds with three sweeping declarations about the nature and station of the Ahlul Bayt: they are the custodians of divine knowledge, the interpreters of divine revelation, and the definitive proof of Allah over all of creation. This statement reflects the Shia theological doctrine of the Imamate — that the Imams hold a unique mediating role between God's guidance and humanity, inheriting the Prophet's authority in preserving and transmitting sacred knowledge.
